name: FlashInfer
notable_features: A kernel library for LLM serving, not a serving engine: attention, sampling and fused-MoE primitives that other engines call into
JIT compilation with a cubin cache and a pluggable JIT cache provider, plus prebuilt flashinfer-cubin artifacts
Default attention backend for SGLang and selectable in vLLM, so it changes those engines' performance more than it provides a runtime of its own
Customizable attention plans and prefill/decode splits; paper at arXiv:2501.01005

Ships three runtime artifact paths as a deliberate packaging tradeoff: flashinfer-python (runtime JIT), flashinfer-jit-cache (prebuilt JIT shared libraries for covered specializations) and flashinfer-cubin (pre-downloaded cubin/header artifacts) - the vendor's stated goal is that a representative workload runs with 'zero runtime JIT and zero runtime artifact downloads' when all three are installed, verified via FLASHINFER_DISABLE_JIT=1 and FLASHINFER_NO_DOWNLOAD=1

That packaging choice has a published constraint worth knowing before planning on it: GitHub Releases caps each release asset at 2 GiB, FlashInfer wheels ship as release assets, and AOT coverage is therefore a tradeoff rather than free - stated in the project's own RFC
hardware_caveats: CUDA-only and sm75+ only - it is explicitly unsupported below compute capability 7.5, which excludes Volta and older

Requires JIT compilation on first use, so cold start and cache-miss environments pay a compile cost; stale caches are a known failure mode and the documented fix is a forced reinstall plus deleting ~/.cache/flashinfer
Not an engine: you cannot serve a model with it alone. Scheduling is 'none' because it owns no scheduler
Kernels are tuned for NVIDIA's architecture; there is no HIP, ROCm, Metal or Vulkan path
When it misbehaves on sm75+ parts, the engines' documented fallback is to switch attention and sampling back to Triton and PyTorch
best_for: Squeezing attention and sampling throughput inside SGLang or vLLM on NVIDIA GPUs
Researching custom attention plans and sampling strategies against a real serving harness
As the default attention path when you have already committed to SGLang
avoid_for: Non-NVIDIA hardware, or NVIDIA parts below sm75
Environments where JIT compilation at runtime is unacceptable
Serving on its own - pair it with an engine
notes: supported_formats is essentially empty by design: it consumes tensors from a host engine rather than loading checkpoints. Included here because it is a genuine, widely deployed GPU inference component that changes engine performance characteristics, and because its sm75 floor is the kind of hardware boundary this knowledge base exists to record. ||| MAINTENANCE (dated fact, GitHub API, 2026-10-04): last commit 2026-10-04 (0 months), latest release v0.7.0.post1 published 2026-09-29, 424 contributors, open_issues_count 1103 (issues PLUS pull requests), NOT archived, 6544 stars. Unusually for a young project, a large contributor base - this is not a single-maintainer dependency. DEPLOYMENT: NO EVIDENCE OF PRODUCTION DEPLOYMENT FOUND as of 2026-10-04 - see [[ev-production-evidence-is-scarce-and-nearly-always-single-site]] for the grading scheme and for why absence of evidence is not evidence of absence. PERFORMANCE: the repo's one and only substantive finding about THIS engine is a cost, not a rate, and it is a cost paid inside requests - see [[ev-jit-compile-freezes-the-engine-mid-request]] and [[ev-jit-cache-key-invalidation]]. FlashInfer's own open RFC #4035 proposes making cold compile time a reported KPI and its measurement table is still unfilled, which is itself the honest state of this engine's performance reporting: there is no published throughput table with load conditions, and this record does not invent one. BUILD COST: measured per-kernel - ~40 s first hit for the dynamic kernel and ~15-18 s per small-m micro-kernel specialization on RTX PRO 6000, REPAID EVERY ENGINE START because the file cache is bypassed; and a general statement of when it repeats, since 'B/tile_v/T/cache flags/pool-strides each key a new compile'.
